final.label: The whole island — 12–18 September
final.note: South, east, north and west including all of Snæfellsnes, with the Húsavík whale boat. Six nights, no camping card, early starts. Day 6 finishes after dark on purpose.

days.title: Golden Circle, then south
days.summary: Straight off the plane into the classics, then down to the south coast.
days.note: Early start pays for itself all week. Shop in Selfoss — last big supermarket before the south coast.

days.title: Every waterfall on the south coast
days.summary: Six waterfalls, two headlands, a black beach and the Klaustur cluster.
days.note: Gljúfrafoss is 600 m from Seljalandsfoss and half of people miss it. The five stops around Kirkjubæjarklaustur are within a kilometre of Route 1 — ten minutes each.

days.title: Glacier lagoon and the south-east corner
days.summary: Svartifoss before breakfast crowds, then the lagoon and Vestrahorn.
days.note: You are camped inside the national park, so Svartifoss is a first-thing walk with nobody on it. Stokksnes is private land, about 1,000 ISK.

days.title: East fjords, Stuðlagil and Mývatn
days.summary: The fjord road, the basalt canyon, then the whole geothermal lake in the evening.
days.note: Stuðlagil's east-bank car park is the one with the good walk down. The Mývatn cluster is done this evening rather than tomorrow, which is what keeps day 6 sane.

days.title: Dettifoss, the whales, then west
days.summary: Dettifoss early, the boat at Húsavík, then Goðafoss and a run west.
days.note: Book the whale trip now — September sailings fill and get cancelled for weather. An afternoon departure leaves the morning for Dettifoss and the lake.

split.note: Both leave from the same harbour, about 100 m apart — regroup on the quay.

options.book: Book ahead. The one big spend of the trip.
For anyone not sailing, or if it blows out.

days.title: North coast to Snæfellsnes
days.summary: Vatnsnes in the morning, then the whole Snæfellsnes loop.
days.note: The monster — expect to finish after dark, which is fine on Route 1 and the 54. Drop Kolugljúfur and Borgarvirki first if you are behind. Grundarfjörður's campsite shut on 15 September, so tonight is Arnarstapi on the south side — which also makes the flight morning short.

days.title: Snæfellsnes south, then the plane
days.summary: Three stops on the doorstep, then a clear run to Keflavík.
days.note: Deliberately short. Aim to be at KEF by 15:00 for the 17:00 flight — you should manage it by lunchtime with an early start.

north.label: The north coast — 12–18 September
north.note: No Golden Circle in this one, and no Vatnsnes. Those hours go north instead — Ásbyrgi, which is eleven minutes of driving, and the Tröllaskagi coast with Siglufjörður and a soak at Grettislaug. Starts in Reykjavík, and Snæfellsnes gets a day and a morning rather than one long push, so nothing finishes in the dark.

days.title: Out of Reykjavík, the whole south coast
days.summary: Six waterfalls, two headlands, a black beach, finishing at the canyon.
days.note: Gljúfrafoss is 600 m from Seljalandsfoss and half of people miss it. Shop in Selfoss — last big supermarket before the south coast.

days.title: Klaustur cluster, Svartifoss and the glacier lagoon
days.summary: Five stops within a kilometre of the road, then the park, the lagoon, Vestrahorn.
days.note: The five stops around Kirkjubæjarklaustur are ten minutes each. Svartifoss is a 45-minute walk up from the Skaftafell car park — you are not camped at the foot of it in this version, so expect company. Stokksnes is private land, about 1,000 ISK.

days.title: East fjords, Stuðlagil and Mývatn
days.summary: The fjord road, the basalt canyon, then the whole geothermal lake in the evening.
days.note: Stuðlagil's east-bank car park is the one with the good walk down, and the 38 km round trip down Jökuldalur is the most expensive single detour in the week — it is the first thing to drop if the weather turns.

days.title: Dettifoss, Ásbyrgi and the whales
days.summary: The Diamond Circle done properly, including the canyon most people drive past.
days.note: Route 862 is paved the whole way from Route 1 north to Route 85, so Dettifoss and Ásbyrgi sit on a through-road rather than an out-and-back — Ásbyrgi costs eleven minutes of driving. Book the whale trip now; September sailings fill and get cancelled for weather. Akureyri's own campsite is not in the OSM extract, so tonight is Vaglaskógur in the forest 20 km east, and Akureyri opens tomorrow.

split.note: Both leave from the same harbour, about 100 m apart — regroup on the quay.

options.book: Book ahead. The one big spend of the trip.
For anyone not sailing, or if it blows out.

days.title: The Tröllaskagi coast
days.summary: Akureyri, then the north coast road instead of Route 1 — Siglufjörður and a soak.
days.note: Route 1 does Akureyri to Blönduós in two hours and shows you nothing. The coast road costs about 78 km and 1.4 h more and is the cheapest unseen ground on the trip. Grettislaug is two stone pots on the shore at Reykir facing Drangey, 17 km up a dead-end road past Sauðárkrókur — the pool Grettir swam ashore to in the saga. No closing time to race, unlike the municipal pool at Hofsós. Bring your own towels. No Vatnsnes today: Hvítserkur is a 68 km spur and you cannot have both peninsulas in one day. v4 takes that one.

days.title: Snæfellsnes, unhurried
days.summary: The whole peninsula with time to stop — Stykkishólmur, Kirkjufell, a lava tube.
days.note: v4 covers this same ground in one 11.7 h push; here it gets a day and a morning. Vatnshellir is a guided 45-minute descent on a fixed tour schedule, about 5,900 ISK a head — turn up for a departure, you cannot just walk in. Grundarfjörður's campsite shut on 15 September, so tonight is Arnarstapi on the south side — which also makes the flight morning short.

days.title: Snæfellsnes south, then the plane
days.summary: Three stops on the doorstep, then a clear run to Keflavík.
days.note: Deliberately short. Aim to be at KEF by 15:00 for the 17:00 flight — you should manage it by lunchtime with an early start.
